      "text": "\n\n\nTo trim this log file effectively while preserving the header and keeping multi-line messages intact, the best approach is to use a small script. \n\nHere are two options to do this depending on what you have installed on your system. **Option 1** uses Python (the most robust for text processing), and **Option 2** uses Windows PowerShell (great if you are on Windows and don\u0027t want to install anything).\n\n### Option 1: Python Script (Recommended)\n\nIf you have Python installed, you can use this script. It reads the file line by line, keeps the header intact, and begins filtering once it detects the date pattern.\n\n1. Save the code below as `trimmer.py`.\n2. Change the `INPUT_FILE` and `OUTPUT_FILE` variables to match your filenames.\n3. Run the script via your terminal: `python trimmer.py`\n\n```python\nimport re\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\n# --- CONFIGURATION ---\nINPUT_FILE \u003d \"logs.txt\"        # Replace with your original file name\nOUTPUT_FILE \u003d \"trimmed.txt\"    # Replace with what you want the new file to be named\nCUTOFF_DATE \u003d \"20/04/2026\"     # DD/MM/YYYY format\n# ---------------------\n\ndef trim_discord_logs(input_file, output_file, cutoff_str):\n    # Parse the cutoff date\n    cutoff_date \u003d datetime.strptime(cutoff_str, \"%d/%m/%Y\")\n    \n    # Regex to catch the start of a message: [DD/MM/YYYY h:mm am/pm]\n    msg_start_pattern \u003d re.compile(r\u0027^\\[(\\d{2}/\\d{2}/\\d{4})\\s+\\d{1,2}:\\d{2}\\s+(?:am|pm|AM|PM)\\]\u0027)\n    \n    with open(input_file, \u0027r\u0027, encoding\u003d\u0027utf-8\u0027) as infile, \\\n         open(output_file, \u0027w\u0027, encoding\u003d\u0027utf-8\u0027) as outfile:\n        \n        in_header \u003d True\n        keep_message \u003d True\n        \n        for line in infile:\n            # Check if the line is the start of a new message\n            match \u003d msg_start_pattern.match(line)\n            \n            if match:\n                in_header \u003d False # We found the first message, header is over\n                \n                # Extract the date and check if it\u0027s on or after our cutoff date\n                date_str \u003d match.group(1)\n                msg_date \u003d datetime.strptime(date_str, \"%d/%m/%Y\")\n                \n                if msg_date \u003e\u003d cutoff_date:\n                    keep_message \u003d True\n                else:\n                    keep_message \u003d False\n            \n            # Write the line if it belongs to the header or to a message we want to keep\n            if in_header or keep_message:\n                outfile.write(line)\n\nif __name__ \u003d\u003d \"__main__\":\n    trim_discord_logs(INPUT_FILE, OUTPUT_FILE, CUTOFF_DATE)\n    print(\"Trimming complete! Check your output file.\")\n```\n\n---\n\n### Option 2: Windows PowerShell\n\nIf you are on Windows and don\u0027t have Python, you can run this script directly in PowerShell. \n\n1. Save the code below as `trimmer.ps1`.\n2. Update the `$inputFile` and `$outputFile` paths.\n3. Right-click the file and select **Run with PowerShell** (or run it via the PowerShell terminal).\n\n```powershell\n# --- CONFIGURATION ---\n$inputFile \u003d \"logs.txt\"\n$outputFile \u003d \"trimmed.txt\"\n$cutoffDate \u003d [datetime]::ParseExact(\"20/04/2026\", \"dd/MM/yyyy\", $null)\n# ---------------------\n\n$inHeader \u003d $true\n$keepMessage \u003d $true\n\nGet-Content $inputFile -Encoding UTF8 | ForEach-Object {\n    # Check if the line matches the date format [DD/MM/YYYY h:mm am/pm]\n    if ($_ -match \"^\\[(\\d{2}/\\d{2}/\\d{4})\\s+\\d{1,2}:\\d{2}\\s+(am|pm|AM|PM)\\]\") {\n        $inHeader \u003d $false\n        $dateStr \u003d $matches[1]\n        \n        # Parse the extracted date\n        $msgDate \u003d [datetime]::ParseExact($dateStr, \"dd/MM/yyyy\", $null)\n        \n        # Determine if we should keep or skip this message\n        if ($msgDate -ge $cutoffDate) {\n            $keepMessage \u003d $true\n        } else {\n            $keepMessage \u003d $false\n        }\n    }\n    \n    # Output the line if it\u0027s header content or valid message content\n    if ($inHeader -or $keepMessage) {\n        $_\n    }\n} | Set-Content $outputFile -Encoding UTF8\n\nWrite-Host \"Trimming complete! Check your output file.\"\n```\n\n### How it works:\n* **Header Preservation:** The code assumes everything at the top of the document (before the first `",
